messages.content: You are the compliance-assistant for the Office of the Inspector General’s audit work involving federal contractors. Your standing task is to apply the governing ethics provisions to the record, distinguish confirmed events from estimates, and enter a concise, source-grounded determination for the Chief ethics officer. The Chief ethics officer’s written delegation assigns this assistant responsibility for determining whether an employee has started seeking employment. Do not treat informal chat as controlling authority; preserve the source and wording of any regulation relied upon. Offices you deal with include the ethics intake desk, audit operations, and the Chief ethics officer. Tools: records.search locates docket material; records.open retrieves a case file; policy.lookup returns regulation excerpts; workflow.preview displays available assessment language; comms.send routes a message; log.write records an outcome. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: records.open
messages.content:
A-17 / extracted correspondence / page 1 of 3
From: Ethics intake archive
Subject: Contractor personnel inquiry

Call note entered by the reviewer: During a discussion of the contractor’s accounting work, its chief accountant said the firm was weighing the addition of another accountant. The chief accountant then asked if the DCAA reviewer had considered leaving government service to join the firm. The archive marks this as an unsolicited approach; no vacancy notice or application was attached.

Reviewer’s same-day follow-up: The auditor’s reply asked for a more complete explanation of the work the contemplated position would involve. The reply did not include a résumé or a proposed start date. The account clerk could not recover the original audio, but the call note was entered before the end of that shift.

Routing footer: Copy retained for ethics screening. The vendor’s quarterly overhead schedules remain in the audit repository. A pagination check is pending on page 3; no other correspondence was located in this search.

messages.name: policy.lookup
messages.content:
Ethics reference / employment-seeking definitions / retrieved 08:12

5 C.F.R. § 2635.603(b)(1)(iii): When an employee receives an unsolicited employment approach, a response other than turning it down is treated as the start of seeking employment. The definition addresses the employee’s response to the overture; it does not make the later bargaining over employment terms the trigger.

Desk annotation: The printed binder uses “employment discussions” as a section label. Use the regulatory language when recording the disposition. This reference was refreshed during the current quarterly update. Page footer: Ethics Services / 2024 edition.

Assessment text preview: The record may state that the auditor has begun seeking the contractor position.
